name: Epic AI (SlicerDicer, etc.)
pros: Embedded in the EHR clinicians already use, no workflow change required
Scale of patient data behind Epic's model training
files: Patient records, clinical notes, and structured EHR data.
value: AI capabilities across Epic's electronic health record, including clinical decision support, ambient documentation (ambient listening that drafts clinical notes), and analytics via SlicerDicer and a range of prediction models. Used by over 350 million patient records' worth of institutions.
engine: Epic's own models and Microsoft Azure AI Services, under Epic's development and validation processes.
latency: Real-time for clinical decision support; batch for analytics.

pricing.model: Within Epic contract, some AI features additional
pricing.includes: Base AI features; ambient documentation is priced separately

quality: Quality is the sector's primary compliance question, not speed. Clinical AI models must be validated on the deployment population before clinical reliance, which is a regulatory requirement in addition to good practice.
tagline: AI across the EHR used by most major US health systems, with regulatory requirements that differ from any other sector.
use_cases: Ambient clinical documentation reducing physician administrative burden
Predictive risk scoring for sepsis, readmission, and care escalation
Population health analytics via SlicerDicer across the patient panel
integrations: Azure AI Services for model execution
HL7 FHIR for external data exchange
governance_note: Healthcare AI operates under a regulatory framework that is categorically different from general enterprise AI: FDA oversight of Software as a Medical Device applies to clinical AI tools that are decision-support for diagnosis or treatment, HIPAA governs all patient data handling, and validation on the deployment population is both a regulatory expectation and a patient safety requirement. The EU AI Act classifies AI used in clinical contexts as high-risk. Before any Epic AI feature is enabled in a clinical setting, the governance question is whether the feature constitutes a SaMD and whether the appropriate validation has been performed. See the healthcare pages in the reference library.
training_optout: Epic's health data terms apply and are structured around HIPAA requirements. Data stays within the health system's Epic environment.
